Testers' agreement and privacy notice (draft 0.1, 11 Nov 2026)

Written by the project's agent for the provider to read and change; no lawyer has checked it (decision of the owner, 4 Nov 2026: no legal review; testers join under an agreement that sets no expectation of any kind). Where a clause says "Proposed", it is a choice the provider has not yet made. The statistics paragraphs repeat what the app's consent screen says (app/src-tauri/src/usage.rs); if either changes, change both.

1. Who and what

"The provider" is Vincenzo Ciancia, vincenzoml@gmail.com. "You" are the person who takes part in the test. "The app" is the unfinished test version of Nearbytes that the provider gives you, on one or more of your devices.

You take part by choice, for no payment, and the provider owes you nothing for it. Either of us may end it at any time, for any reason, without notice (clause 9).

2. What the app is, and what you must not expect

  • The app is unfinished and offered for a limited time, only to research how well device-to-device sync works. It is not a product and not a service. It does not comply with the EU Cyber Resilience Act and must not be used for anything else.
  • It can lose data, show wrong data, stop working, or stop syncing, without warning and without any promise of a fix.
  • Keep nothing in it that you cannot afford to lose. Keep your own copy of everything you put in it.
  • You accept these defects knowingly, as a separate step from the rest of this agreement: the app asks you to confirm it on first start (the consent screen).
  • Nothing in this agreement or around it sets an expectation of any kind: not of availability, speed, support, fixes, continuity, compatibility between versions, or that the test or the project continues.

3. Licence

The provider lets you use the app, for free, on your own devices, only for taking part in this test. You may not sell it, offer it to others as a service, take it apart to remove its limits, or use it for anything unlawful. The app's source code keeps its own licence terms; this agreement gives you no right beyond using the app for the test. (Proposed: the provider names the licence of the code here before the first outside tester joins.)

4. Your data and your content

  • What you put into your hubs (messages, files, names of hubs) is yours. The provider does not ask for it and cannot read it: it is encrypted on your devices with keys that never leave them, and the provider never decrypts anything anyone puts in the app for the purposes of the test.
  • Your hubs' secrets and your list live on your devices. If you lose them, nobody can recover them, the provider included.
  • You are responsible for what you put in hubs you share. Do not put in anything unlawful, or anything you have no right to share.

5. Carrying other people's encrypted data

To work, devices of a hub carry and pass on blocks of that hub's data for each other, and the app may keep encrypted blocks of hubs on your device that you are not a member of (so that others' devices can get them while theirs are offline). Those blocks are encrypted; you cannot read them and the app does not let you. They use some of your device's storage and network, within limits the app sets itself, and are evicted first when space is short. By taking part you agree that your device carries them. You may leave the test at any time, and the app then stops.

6. Statistics the app sends to the provider

While you take part, the app sends the provider pseudonymous statistics: platform and version, how and how fast devices connect, how many connections each installation has, how long changes take to arrive, updates that failed, and errors shown on screen, with every number, address, path and key removed from their messages. They are tied to a random number created when you take part, never to your name, and never include keys, addresses, hub names or anything inside hubs. Every record also holds that random number, when it was made, the app's version, and the version and time of the notice you accepted. The statistics are sent sealed so that only the provider can read them, and will only ever be used for this research.

The provider keeps the statistics of each installation until the end of the test, and at most 24 months after they were collected; an installation's are deleted after 6 months in which it sent nothing. Only anonymous totals are kept after that. The list of what each kind of record holds is in the app ("What this version collects").

7. What the meeting points can see

Devices find each other through a "meeting point", a small service run by the provider on a cloud provider's network (Cloudflare). It passes the offers and answers that let two devices connect, and holds no message and no file. While the test runs, the meeting point is in a debug mode: it may log that a device joined, which short prefix of a hub (eight hexadecimal digits, not the hub's secret) was joined, which kinds of messages passed and how many bytes, and the browser's name and version when the web app is used. This debug mode is switched off, and its logs deleted, before the release that ends the test phase. Your IP address is visible to the meeting point and to the cloud provider as it is to any web service you connect to.

8. Updates

The app updates itself while the test runs, and you cannot stay on an older version for ever: an update can change how the app behaves, and what it collects (you are asked again if the notice changes). If something goes wrong with a test version, an update included, the provider warns you on https://nearbytes-app.github.io/warnings/, which does not depend on the app: look at it if the app misbehaves or does not start.

9. Leaving, and the end of the test

  • You can leave at any time with "Leave the test" in the app: sending stops, the records waiting on your device are deleted, and the provider is asked to delete every record of your installation (the request reaches the provider when your device next meets the provider's, so it can take time). Uninstalling the app removes its data from your device.
  • The provider can end your part, or the whole test, at any time. At the end of the test the provider stops the meeting points, deletes the statistics as in clause 6, and the app stops working or stays as a local program, as the provider announces on the page in clause 8.
  • Export: your files are plain files you put in; the app can save them to your device. Do that before the test ends. Nothing else is exported, because nothing else is held about you.

10. Your rights over the statistics

The statistics are tied to a random number, not to you, so the provider cannot know which ones are yours unless you give the number (it is shown in the app, under "This machine"). With that number you may ask the provider, at the contact in clause 1, to show or delete them; deleting is also what "Leave the test" asks for. You may complain to the Italian data protection authority (Garante per la protezione dei dati personali) if you believe your data are handled wrongly. The provider is the controller of the statistics.

11. Warranty and liability

The app and the test are given "as they are", with no warranty of any kind. To the extent the law allows, the provider is not liable for any loss, including lost data, lost time, or damage to your devices, arising from the app or the test. The law does not allow excluding liability for some things (for example for wilful misconduct or gross negligence, or for death or personal injury); this agreement does not try to.

12. Law and courts

Proposed: Italian law governs this agreement; for a dispute, the courts of the provider's place of residence, except where the law gives you the right to go to your own. The provider decides this before the first outside tester joins.

13. The clauses you confirm separately

You confirm, each on its own, that you have read and accept: clause 2 (the defects and no expectation), clause 5 (carrying others' encrypted data), clause 7 (the meeting point's debug mode), clause 11 (warranty and liability) and clause 12 (law and courts). The app's consent screen asks for clause 2 and clause 6 at first start; the others are confirmed on this page when the provider invites you.

Open for the provider to decide

  • The licence of the app's code (clause 3).
  • The law and courts (clause 12): Italian law and the provider's courts are proposed, nothing more.
  • How the separate confirmations in clause 13 are collected (a link in the invitation, the consent screen, or a reply).
  • Whether the provider's contact stays a personal address (clause 1).
